volume.tooltip: Speaker level (−∞…0 dB). 0 dB is unity. Default −3 dB. Old patches that stored 0…1 linear Volume are converted on load. Type a dB value (or −inf).

pan.tooltip: Stereo balance after Mono is summed in. 0 = unchanged (Mono to both). −1 = left only. +1 = right only.

darkness.tooltip: Maximum randomized rectangular pulse width. 1 = bright velvet noise; higher values = wider rectangular pulses for natural 6 dB/oct high-frequency damping.

tailDarkness.tooltip: Darkness at the end of the tail. The widest pulse grows from Darkness at the first tap to this at the last, so the tail gets darker as it goes, like a room where the highs die first. The tail's level stays set by Amp Decay; this only changes its colour. 0 = off (the whole tail uses Darkness).

stereoSpread.tooltip: 0% = identical L/R tap offsets (mono). 100% = independent L/R taps for decorrelated stereo.

seed.tooltip: RNG seed for tap positions, signs, and pulse widths. Same seed = identical taps.

highFreq.tooltip: Sweep start frequency (the click). Latched on each Trigger. Clamped to 50 Hz ... half the sample rate.

lowFreq.tooltip: Frequency the sweep settles toward (a tuned body). 0 = keeps falling. Latched on each Trigger.

sweepTime.tooltip: Time to fall from High Freq to Low Freq + 50 Hz. Latched on each Trigger. From Robin Schmidt's SweepKicker, RS-MET.

chirp.tooltip: Tail power of the sweep. + holds the highs longer, then drops fast. - drops fast at first, then lingers low. Acts at once. From Robin Schmidt's SweepKicker, RS-MET.

chirpShape.tooltip: Attack knee vs decay at the same tail power. + keeps the start frequency a little longer, - rounds the knee. Acts at once. From Robin Schmidt's SweepKicker, RS-MET.

wave.tooltip: SawSine: fat saw (Morph 1) to sine (0). TriSine: hyperbolic tent, triangle (1) to sine (0). SawTri: saw (1) to triangle (0). Morph 1 is high-frequency content.

waveShape.tooltip: 1 = high-frequency end, 0 = low-frequency end. Modulate 1→0 as the kick falls. TriSine floors tent softness by pitch so the triangle end does not alias like a naive tent.

phase.tooltip: Start phase offset. Trigger hard-resets the oscillator to this phase. 0 = clean start at zero. +-0.25 = starts at a peak: hard click.

decay.tooltip: Amplitude envelope: seconds to fall 60 dB (T60) after a hit. Drives the 0–1 output and the Kick level. Acts at once.

amplitude.tooltip: Kick output level. Does not scale the 0–1 output.

voices.tooltip: How many stolen tails can fade at once. Only one kick is live; a retrigger fades the previous over Fade Time. Decay does not stretch Fade Time.

voiceFade.tooltip: On: a stolen voice fades out over Fade Time instead of cutting (no retrigger click, including Voices 1). Off: hard cut.

algorithm.tooltip: Hat design. 808: six PolyBLEP squares (205-800 Hz) through the 7.1 kHz band-pass and a high-pass. 606: six squares (606 tuning, by ear) into a resonant high-pass. FM: metallic FM carrier ring-modulated by a pulse pair, high-passed. Noise: band-passed white noise. Knobs keep their values when you switch.

tune.tooltip: Metal pitch scale, 1 = stock. 808 / 606: all six squares. FM: every operator. Noise: band-pass centre (8 kHz x Tune).

tone.tooltip: Brightness. 808 / 606: band-pass and high-pass move together, one octave down (0) to one up (1). FM: modulation index 2 -> 12 and high-pass. Noise: band-pass Q 0.5 -> 5.

closedDecay.tooltip: Closed hit decay: seconds to fall 60 dB (T60).

openDecay.tooltip: Open hit decay: seconds to fall 60 dB (T60).

metal.tooltip: Metallic source <-> white noise; 1 = all metal (stock 808 / 606). Noise algorithm: band-passed (1) <-> raw (0) noise.

amplitude.tooltip: Output level. Does not scale Env.

mix.tooltip: Dry/wet balance on the Mix outputs (not a wet-only path).

diffusionSize.tooltip: Longest diffusion delay line, in ms (each line gets a random fraction of it).

delaySize.tooltip: Length of the 2 main reverb delay taps, in ms.

recycle.tooltip: Feedback amount for the reverb tail.

lfoAmplitude.tooltip: Delay modulation depth as a fraction of each line's own delay length (0.1 = each line swings by 10% of its length).

lfoBaseSpeed.tooltip: Delay modulation LFO rate in Hz (base rate; Mod(~)Vary slows some lines down).

lfoVariation.tooltip: Spread of modulation speed between delay lines: up to this many ms of extra LFO period per line. 0 = all lines modulate at the same speed.

lfoStyle.tooltip: Delay-time modulator. Parabol = original Sabrina cyclic wow. FBM = fractal Brownian flutter (same family as SoEm Reverb / Delay).

delayTapMod.tooltip: Modulation depth multiplier on the 2 main (non-diffuse) delay taps. 1 = original Sabrina, 0 = those taps hold a fixed length (diffusion keeps modulating), 2 = double depth.

seed.tooltip: Randomizes the delay line pattern. Same seed always reproduces the same reverb character.

volume1.tooltip: Pair 1 level (−∞…+12 dB). 0 dB is unity.

volume2.tooltip: Pair 2 level (−∞…+12 dB). 0 dB is unity.

volume3.tooltip: Pair 3 level (−∞…+12 dB). 0 dB is unity.

volume4.tooltip: Pair 4 level (−∞…+12 dB). 0 dB is unity.

pan1.tooltip: Pair 1 stereo balance. 0 = unchanged. −1 = left only. +1 = right only.

pan2.tooltip: Pair 2 stereo balance. 0 = unchanged. −1 = left only. +1 = right only.

pan3.tooltip: Pair 3 stereo balance. 0 = unchanged. −1 = left only. +1 = right only.

pan4.tooltip: Pair 4 stereo balance. 0 = unchanged. −1 = left only. +1 = right only.

amplitude.tooltip: Master gain after all four pairs (−∞…+12 dB). 0 dB is unity.

volume1.tooltip: Pair 1 level (−∞…+12 dB). 0 dB is unity.

volume2.tooltip: Pair 2 level (−∞…+12 dB). 0 dB is unity.

volume3.tooltip: Pair 3 level (−∞…+12 dB). 0 dB is unity.

volume4.tooltip: Pair 4 level (−∞…+12 dB). 0 dB is unity.

pan1.tooltip: Pair 1 stereo balance. 0 = unchanged. −1 = left only. +1 = right only.

pan2.tooltip: Pair 2 stereo balance. 0 = unchanged. −1 = left only. +1 = right only.

pan3.tooltip: Pair 3 stereo balance. 0 = unchanged. −1 = left only. +1 = right only.

pan4.tooltip: Pair 4 stereo balance. 0 = unchanged. −1 = left only. +1 = right only.

amplitude.tooltip: Master gain after all four pairs (−∞…+12 dB). 0 dB is unity.

rate.tooltip: Clock rate in Hz. Wired ƒ cancels Rate (absolute Hz), same as oscillators.

pulseStart.tooltip: Where in the cycle the gate goes high. Quantized to whole samples.

pulseEnd.tooltip: Where in the cycle the gate goes low. Quantized to whole samples.

upShape.tooltip: Rising glide curve. Lin = constant rate. Log = fast start, eases in. Exp = slow start, finishes quickly. Smooth = slow start and end.

downShape.tooltip: Falling glide curve. Lin = constant rate. Log = fast start, eases in. Exp = slow start, finishes quickly. Smooth = slow start and end.

upTime.tooltip: Seconds to reach a higher target from the current value (any amplitude — Hz, CV, audio). 0 = instant.

downTime.tooltip: Seconds to reach a lower target from the current value (any amplitude). 0 = instant.

bias.tooltip: Offset added before slew (0…1). Hidden by default — show it to step the target by hand.

amplitude.tooltip: Scale and invert. 0 = mute, +1 = unity, −1 = invert. Bipolar rational is finer around 0.

octave.tooltip: Transpose quantized pitch and ƒ by whole octaves.

semitones.tooltip: Transpose quantized pitch and ƒ by integer semitones.

frequency.tooltip: Default slider 0…20 kHz. Pitch MOD can run down through 0. Thru-zero: enable Bipolar on Frequency (domain-add MOD). Domain min/max are slider guides.

morph.tooltip: 0…1 width/duty. 0.5 = center / 50%. Affects Trisaw, Analog Square (same-direction peaks), Trisaw Center (opposing peaks toward saw), Pulse, and Center Square (pulse grows from mid-cycle — not a stepped square). Morph MOD jack on the param row.

amplitude.tooltip: Output level. Slider 0…1 = full-scale bipolar wave. Post-MOD stays in min…max (Gate+Toggle cannot boost past Amp max).

frequency.tooltip: Pitch of the pluck: loop delay D = fs/f (fractional, Thiran). When ƒ is wired, that Hz is the pitch (absolute). Unwired uses this knob (Hz).

decay.tooltip: Seconds for the ring to fall to 1/e (about -8.7 dB), same law as Comb Resonator: loop gain g = exp(-D/(τ·fs)). T60 is about 6.9 x Decay.

damping.tooltip: One-pole lowpass in the loop (Karplus-Strong). 0 = bright, every partial rings for Decay. Higher = the top partials die faster than the body (pow instead of pong).

invert.tooltip: + = all harmonics of Frequency. − = inverted loop: odd harmonics of Frequency/2, hollow and an octave down.

shape.tooltip: Exciter fired on each Trigger edge, one burst shorter than the period. Bump = one smooth hump (Soft widens it). Triangle = one band-limited triangle cycle. Saw = one band-limited saw cycle (DSF rolloff). Noise = a filtered noise burst. Every shape has its DC removed, so the loop never drifts.

soft.tooltip: Softness of the exciter, latched at each hit. Bump: 1 = gentle hump, 0 = narrow punchy spike. Triangle / Saw: 1 = sine, 0 = sharp corners (geometric harmonic rolloff, like DSF Bright). Noise: 1 = dark, 0 = white.

width.tooltip: Exciter length as a fraction of one period (1/Frequency), latched at each hit. Narrow = bright tick or pong, wide = round pow or thump. Tied to the period, so the timbre follows pitch. Kept under one period so the burst never overlaps its own echo.

retrigger.tooltip: What a new hit does to a ring that is still sounding. Stack = adds into it (re-plucking a ringing string). Choke = fades the old ring out over 2 ms, clears it, then rings fresh.

level.tooltip: Output level. The first pass of the loop is the exciter itself, so each hit peaks near Level x velocity at any Frequency or Decay.
